title: Microgrids
text:
Microgrids

A microgrid is a local group of generators, batteries and loads that can run connected to the main grid or on its own as an “island”.

Hospitals, military bases and remote villages use microgrids so that the lights stay on when the wider network fails. A controller decides when to import power, when to export it and when to disconnect.

Solar panels and batteries are the most common building blocks, often with a diesel or gas generator as backup.
Falling battery prices have made island mode practical for many more sites over the last decade.
